dish.title: Turkish Mücver: Zucchini-Feta Fritters with Garlic Yogurt and Tomato-Cucumber Salad

recipe_version.title: Turkish Mücver: Zucchini-Feta Fritters with Garlic Yogurt and Tomato-Cucumber Salad
recipe_version.description: Grated zucchini, squeezed dry and mixed with feta, scallions, dill, mint, eggs, flour, and red pepper flakes, shallow-fried into golden fritters. Served with cool garlic yogurt flecked with dill and a tomato, cucumber, and red onion salad dressed with lemon and olive oil.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1 tsp zucchini, 1/4 tsp yogurt, 1/4 tsp salad

ingredients.name: feta
ingredients.display_name: feta made with microbial or vegetable rennet

ingredients.name: fresh dill
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp yogurt, 2 tbsp to scatter, the rest in the batter

ingredients.name: Aleppo or mild red pepper flakes
ingredients.display_name: Aleppo or mild red pepper flakes

steps.title: Grate and salt the zucchini
steps.body: Coarsely grate the zucchini on a box grater, toss it with 1 tsp salt in a colander set in the sink, and leave it to drain 10 minutes; the draining runs inside step 2 (overlap stated).

steps.title: Prep the rest
steps.body: Crumble the feta, slice the scallions, and chop the dill and mint. Stir the garlic, 1 tbsp of the dill, and 1/4 tsp salt into the yogurt. Dice the tomatoes and cucumber, slice the red onion, and juice the lemon.

steps.title: Squeeze and mix
steps.body: A handful at a time, wring the zucchini very dry in a clean towel and drop it into the large bowl. Mix in the feta, scallions, the remaining dill and mint except 2 tbsp of each, the eggs, flour, and pepper flakes to a thick, spoonable batter.

steps.title: Dress the salad
steps.body: Toss the tomatoes, cucumber, and red onion with the lemon juice, olive oil, and 1/4 tsp salt.

steps.title: Shallow-fry the fritters
steps.body: Heat 2/3 cup neutral oil (about 1/8 inch) in a 12-inch skillet over medium until it shimmers, about 3 minutes. Drop in 6 mounds of batter, 1/3 cup each, and flatten to 3 1/2-inch rounds. Cook until deep golden and set through, turning once, about 8 minutes per batch. Drain on a rack. Add the remaining 2/3 cup oil, heat it about 1 minute, and shallow-fry the rest of the batter (2 batches, 12 fritters).

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Plate 3 fritters each, scatter the reserved dill and mint over them, and add a spoonful of garlic yogurt and the salad alongside.

scaling_notes.1: A quarter of everything (3 fritters) in one batch in a 10-inch skillet with about 1/2 cup oil (1/8 inch).
scaling_notes.2: Half of everything (6 fritters) in one batch in the 12-inch skillet with 2/3 cup oil (1/8 inch).
scaling_notes.4: As written (12 fritters, 2 batches, 2/3 cup oil each).
do_not_scale: oil depth: about 1/8 inch whatever the batch: 2/3 cup in a 12-inch skillet, about 1/2 cup in a 10-inch skillet
squeezing: the zucchini must be squeezed very dry whatever the batch size, or the fritters will not hold

coverage_contribution: A vegetarian fritter dinner; zucchini has no lead in the catalog. Turkish meals in the catalog are lahmacun and iskender, both lamb.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with japanese-okonomiyaki: small herb-feta zucchini fritters with yogurt, not a cabbage pancake with mayo and sauce. Compared with shallow-fried-green-tomatoes: grated zucchini batter, not cornmeal-coated tomato slices. Compared with greek-spanakopita: fritters, not a phyllo pie, though both use feta and dill. Compared with turkish-lahmacun: vegetarian, no lamb flatbread.
